meta.name: Brewery-kit CBD extraction (10 bbl jacketed)
meta.subtitle: standard 10 bbl jacketed brewery equipment re-purposed: mash-tun extraction, unitank crystallisation, brite-tank storage, with a media column, a 10 µm–0.01 µm membrane cascade and a low-energy RO
meta.purpose: Extract and isolate CBD from hemp biomass on ordinary 10 bbl jacketed brewery kit — nothing bespoke — with every media, membrane and membrane-position choice computed and cited rather than guessed.
meta.basis: one charge: 120 kg biomass, 960 L carrier, per the balancer defaults; the client's assay replaces the feedstock numbers (A-02)

materials.name: Carrier blend (assumed 70/30)
materials.note: the ratio is assumption A-01 until the client confirms it

media.name: Molecular sieve 13X
media.function: water plus CO2 and light organics

vessels.name: Extraction vessel (10 bbl jacketed mash tun)
vessels.type: jacketed vessel with false bottom and rake
vessels.note: US brewery barrel = 117.35 L; 10 bbl working volume 1,190 L

vessels.name: Carrier day tank (20 bbl brite tank)
Mother liquor tank (10 bbl jacketed brite tank)
Recovered carrier tank (20 bbl brite tank)

isolation.note: bed per media card; sight glasses both ends

vessels.name: Membrane skid
vessels.type: staged cartridge housings, 10 um to 0.01 um
vessels.note: position before and/or after the media column is a setting, not hardware

vessels.name: Low-energy RO skid
vessels.note: water service and aqueous waste; solvent loop only after S-13 is answered

connections.line: through the 3A/13X sieve stack, carrier return

process.name: Extraction with circulation
process.note: S-103 is internal recirculation through the false bottom, not a boundary crossing

streams.name: Extraction circulation
streams.note: 4 vessel turnovers per hour through the false bottom

streams.name: Spent media bed
streams.note: carbon and clay are single-use; sieves and packing stay in service

streams.name: Aqueous waste / glycol make-up feed
streams.note: the RO's service is water, not solvent - S-13

steps.text: Charge the carrier from the 20 bbl brite tank to the extraction vessel at 2 degC under nitrogen.
steps.acceptance: 960 L charged; oxygen below 2 % before agitation starts.

steps.text: Circulate the miscella through the false bottom at 4 turnovers per hour for 2 h at the temperature the operating point sets.
steps.acceptance: circulation rate 4,800 L/h; temperature within 1 K of the set point for the full hold.

steps.text: Pass the miscella through the membrane skid in the configured position; record differential pressure per stage.
steps.acceptance: differential pressure under 1.4 bar per housing; flux recorded at start and end.

steps.text: Pass the miscella through the media column at the dose the operating point sets; never exceed 2x the standard dose without a re-verification.
steps.acceptance: colour removal within 5 % of the predicted value; cannabinoid loss inside the published band.

steps.text: Polish through the 0.2 um and 0.01 um stages to the crystalliser.
steps.acceptance: filter effluent visibly clear; flux above the minimum on the datasheet.

steps.text: Crystallise at -40 degC for 8 h with the scraper running.
steps.acceptance: jacket at -45 degC; crystalliser contents at -40 degC for the full hold.

steps.text: Draw the mother liquor to the jacketed brite tank at -20 degC.
steps.acceptance: crystal slurry to isolation; mother liquor transfer complete.

steps.text: Evaporate the carrier from the mother liquor at the vacuum the operating point sets.
steps.acceptance: boiling temperature within 2 K of the Antoine prediction at the set vacuum.

steps.text: Condense the carrier vapour in the four-shell bank at -20 degC.
steps.acceptance: condensate flow steady; vent scrubber receiving.

steps.text: Dry the recovered carrier through the 3A/13X sieve stack and return it to the day tank.
steps.acceptance: water under 200 ppm at the return.

steps.text: Run the RO on water service only until S-13 is answered in writing by the membrane maker.
steps.acceptance: permeate conductivity within the element datasheet; no solvent in the feed.

notes.text: The media column's bed is chosen on the media tab; carbon and clay are single use, sieves and packing stay in service. Record the bed in the batch record before the pass.
The RO is in the plant for water polish and aqueous waste. It does not see carrier until the maker clears ethanol service (S-13).

simulation.note: the sliders drive this module directly; every coefficient carries a source

sources.citation: NIST Chemistry WebBook, Antoine parameters (ethanol Kretschmer & Wiebe 1949; n-pentane Osborn & Douslin 1974)
Experimental solubility of cannabidiol (CBD) in different organic solvents, Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 2023, 62(31), 12356 - measured 253.1-310.1 K
J. Am. Oil Chem. Soc. (2021) 99:525 - ethanol vs lower-boiling solvents for terpenoids and cannabinoids from hemp inflorescence
CannaLabs Consulting, independent CRC media comparison - carbon 85-95 % colour at 8-15 % cannabinoid strip; bentonite 70-90 % pesticides at low loss
Extraction Magazine (2021), The rise of in-line color remediation; MJBizDaily (2022) - media in commercial use: silica, bentonite, carbon, magnesium silicate
DuPont FilmTec XLE-4040 low-energy RO element - approx 2,600 GPD, >=99 % NaCl rejection, 150 psi test; water service
CRC Handbook - enthalpy of vaporisation: ethanol 838 kJ/kg, n-pentane 358 kJ/kg at the normal boiling point
10 bbl brewery kit convention - US barrel 117.35 L; dimple jacket rating 3 bar; brite-tank PRV 30-45 psi

assumptions.text: The carrier blend is 70 % ethanol and 30 % n-pentane by mass; the ratio is an assumption until the client confirms it.
Feedstock defaults for the balancer: 120 kg biomass per charge, 8 wt % CBD, 10 % moisture. The client's assay replaces all three.
Wax and lipid fraction 8 % of dry biomass; cold extraction retains about 55 % of it. Both are assumptions, not measurements.
Crystal targets (62 % purity, 88 % recovery of CBD into the crystal) are carried from the specification, not measured on this kit.
Carrier recovery 96 % through evaporation and condensation; the loss figure follows from it.
Evaporation spreads over 4 h; the duty figure scales inversely with that cycle time.

evidence.note: topics the design leans on, with what was retrieved; thin evidence is marked thin

E-01.topic: CBD solubility vs temperature in ethanol
E-01.why: the temperature slider's effect is anchored to measured solubility, not to habit

E-02.query: hemp extract remediation carbon silica bentonite cannabinoid loss
E-02.why: the sorbent slider's loss column cites measured ranges

E-03.why: the 0.01 um stage's value must be shown, not assumed

E-04.why: S-13 stays open until the manufacturer answers

E-05.query: ethanol boiling point vacuum falling film evaporator duty
E-05.why: the vacuum slider's boiling point is Antoine, verified in tests

safety.note: Every item here is a question to close, with a rule and an owner. Nothing is signed off until the owner says so in the record.

questions.rule: the carrier blend is flammable; the extraction and evaporation rooms are Class I Division 1 or 2 zones per the electrical classification survey
questions.question: has the electrical classification been surveyed and signed for the exact rooms this kit occupies?
questions.why: brewery kit was built for a non-flammable process; the room classification may not have been done

questions.rule: dimple jackets on brewery vessels are typically rated 3 bar (43.5 psi); operate with margin
questions.question: is the jacket pressure the operating point sets inside the nameplate rating of every vessel, including the old ones?
questions.why: second-hand brewery kit does not always carry its original nameplate

questions.rule: every brite tank keeps its PRV, set at or below the vessel rating
questions.question: when were the PRVs last tested, and are they set below the vessel MAWP?
questions.why: a blocked PRV on a tank with nitrogen blanket is a real over-pressure path

questions.rule: confined-space entry rules around any vessel with a nitrogen blanket
questions.question: who signs the confined-space permit, and is a gas meter at the manway before entry?
questions.why: the plant blankets with nitrogen; the hazard is invisible

questions.rule: the -45 degC crystalliser jacket is a cryogenic burn surface; glycol at -45 degC is not food-safe coolant
questions.question: are the cold surfaces insulated and labelled, and is the glycol loop closed with a spill plan?
questions.why: brewery glycol normally runs near 0 degC; this loop runs far colder

questions.rule: carbon, clay, silica and sieve dusts are nuisance-to-irritant dusts; handle with extraction or a respirator
questions.question: is the media charging step done with dust control, and are spent beds disposed of per their adsorbed load?
questions.why: charging a CRC column is dusty; spent carbon carries adsorbed organics

questions.rule: spent carbon and clay carry adsorbed cannabinoids and pesticides; disposal follows the hazardous-waste determination
questions.question: has a waste determination been done on each spent bed, per media?
questions.why: SCC never takes title; the broker arranges carriers and DOT labelling

questions.rule: cartridge membranes are specified for the chemistry they see
questions.question: are the 10 um to 0.01 um cartridge materials rated for ethanol and the blend?
questions.why: polypropylene and PTFE are usually fine; the verification is still owed

questions.rule: polyamide RO elements are not rated for high-ethanol service
questions.question: S-13 restated: has the membrane maker confirmed ethanol compatibility in writing before the RO sees carrier?
questions.why: the RO is in the plant for water; the temptation to run solvent through it is the risk

questions.rule: copper packing binds sulphur but corrodes in acidic ethanol streams and adds copper traces
questions.question: is copper in the loop only where the product spec tolerates it, and is the pickling waste handled as metal-bearing waste?
questions.why: copper is a distillery habit; it is not free of consequences here

questions.rule: the 96 % carrier recovery target leaves 4 % to capture; vent paths go through the scrubber
questions.question: are all vents routed to SC-101, and is the scrubber carbon bed on a breakthrough schedule?
questions.why: the evaporation vent is the plant's largest VOC path

questions.rule: every operating point, media bed and membrane position is recorded per batch
questions.question: does the batch record capture the slider values as set, not as intended?
questions.why: the studio changes the operating point in seconds; the record must show what actually ran

questions.rule: written manufacturer clearance before solvent service
questions.question: has the maker of the 4040 elements confirmed ethanol compatibility in writing?
questions.why: this is the single most tempting wrong turn in the polish skid

questions.rule: know what the vessel last held before it holds carrier
questions.question: is there a documented cleaning and change-of-service record for every brewery vessel re-purposed here?
questions.why: brewery kit may carry brewing aids, caustic or yeast residues that end up in the extract
